content.comment_body: Hi, can anyone provide the correct approach to combine variable =[product_name]VAR("ID") with trend direction TD/TR in an Excel spreadsheet? I need to generate a table showing temperature sensor data versus time on a single sheet. Is this possible? Regards.

I conducted a test with an analog signal. I connected the AI1 of the [product_name] base module to a controllable 0-10V signal and set this up in the [product_name] program as PT100 / 1000 in the analog amplifier. The output value from the analog amplifier was mapped to VW0, and these VW0 values were logged (see video at [url]). For me, the correct syntax is "= [product_name]VARLS ("VW0" ; "TD")". According to the manual, it suggests "= [product_name]VARLS ("VW0" , "TD")", which does not work for me. It only works with a semicolon instead of a comma, and importantly, a space must follow the semicolon.
Hello everyone, I also performed a test using a chart and it is functioning correctly. See the attachment.

Thank you very much! However, I have another question: Is there any way to increase the data collection beyond 100 entries in the History data limit? I need to collect a larger amount of data in a graph. Is it possible to save the data log in separate cells for three variables (without using commas)? Regards.

Have you checked the operating instructions for the [product_name] Access Tool? If you need more rows, you should create a log file. This would be a CSV file, which can store multiple variables in separate columns for each log entry. A CSV file can hold up to 20,000 rows.

I am unable to view the trend values. I followed the procedure in the previously posted video, except I changed the variable length from VW0 to VD0 as per my configuration. Attached is an image. [user_name]
Please re-read my previous post. I wrote: [product_name]VAR LS ("VW0" , "TD") and used all capital letters.

The arguments L and S or using capital letters do not matter, nor does the space between "ID" and "TD" or "TR". The semicolon ";" is essential, so the online help is incorrect when it says to use a comma ",". The issue seems related to the version of Excel. When the screenshot was taken, [product_name] Access Tool was running on Excel H&B 2010. I tried Excel H&B 2013, and it worked fine with the same function =logovar("VD"; "TD"). Thanks again. [user_name]
For me, it works without any issues...

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced inconsistent results when integrating [company_name] [product_name] data into Excel using the [product_name] Access Tool, especially with functions for trend analysis and data logging. Main challenges included syntax mismatches in formulas, misleading documentation related to delimiters (comma versus semicolon), difficulties expanding historical logging capacity beyond 100 records, and varying behavior depending on the Excel version. While some users struggled to access trend data, others succeeded by correcting syntax and switching Excel versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for easy integration of [product_name] data with Excel, precise and reliable documentation about correct formula usage, the ability to collect and chart extensive datasets, and efficient workflows for logging multiple variables in separate spreadsheet cells.
